MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ADJOURNED MEETING
  November 14, 2022

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates was called to order at 7:00 p.m. at City of Rolling Hills Estates Council Chambers,
  4045 Palos Verdes Dr. N., Rolling Hills Estates, California, by CHAIR CIAROLLA.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR CIAROLLA led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Pope, Ciarolla, Romanelli, Persichina, and Bain

  Commissioners Absent:  McCormick and Retz

  City Staff Present:  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson
  Community Services Coordinator Matt Morrow
  4.  PRESENTATION

  A.  SOUTH COAST BOTANIC GARDENS ACTIVITY UPDATE

  The Community Relations Manager for the South Coast Botanic Gardens
  Stephanie Yinger gave an activity update regarding current and upcoming events
  at the garden.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN commended the garden for its creativity in its programming and
  asked how the children’s garden was progressing. Ms. Yinger stated that the
  children's garden was coming along and probably would not start until January and
  will take about a year and a half for completion.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked if there had been any discussions regarding the
  Hills Are Alive 5k/10k going back through the garden. COMMISSIONER
  PERSICHINA stated that there were no plans to go back through the garden with
  the race. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas confirmed that there has been
  no contact with the garden regarding the race.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN asked how community relations were currently regarding the
  concerns regarding the Disco Oasis event that was held earlier in the year. Ms.
  Yinger stated that she had been in communication with the public and heard both

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
November 14, 2022
   sides regarding the event, and as of that point there is no intention of having a Disco
  Oasis event in the next year.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked if anyone from the garden was at the PV Street
  Fair. Ms. Yinger stated that the Garden had two booths at the street fair and that
  she was present both days. She also stated that the booths were a great
  promotional opportunity at the Fair and that they received around 25-30 new
  memberships for the garden.

  5.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF OCTOBER
  18, 2022

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  POPE to:

  APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  October 18, 2022.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  6.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  NONE.

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  “BUTCHER PARK” NAMING PROCESS (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of the “Butcher
  Park” naming process. She stated that the City will be surveying the residents
  regarding the naming of “Butcher Park”. She added that the park project plans are
  complete, and the City is planning to go out to bid in April 2023 with construction of
  the park planned for July/August 2023 with completion in August/September 2023.
  She also stated that Staff will return to the Commission in January with a list of
  names to review to make a recommendation to City Council after the survey
  outreach.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked how wide the survey would be released
  among the community. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas responded that
  the survey would be available for all residents via eblasts and social media as well
  as sent to all Commissioners. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI also asked if the
  naming policy would be attached to the survey to give guidance to those suggesting
  a name. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas stated that maybe a link could

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
November 14, 2022
   be included to the survey with the naming policy, or a scaled down version of the
  policy could be attached to the survey. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI agreed that
  those would be good options to allow the community the ability to submit choices
  that are aligned with the City’s naming policy.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked if the survey would remain anonymous or would
  there be a way for someone to add their personal information, location of residence,
  or comments. Community Services Supervisor stated that the City intended for the
  survey to be simple, but that it could include those options in the survey.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA agreed to attaching the naming policy to the
  survey stating that it would be beneficial to the participants of the survey.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked why the park was currently called “Butcher Park”.
  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA stated that Mr. Butcher owned a lot of the property
  around the City and recalled that he donated the section listed as “Butcher Park”.
  CHAIR CIAROLLA asked if he should be the one to name the park since he owned
  and donated the property. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated that many did not
  really understand why the name “Butcher” was assigned to the park, but now that
  it was stated that Mr. Butcher donated that section of his property asked why it could
  not be named Butcher Park. CHAIR CIAROLLA suggested that the City should
  honor the person who donated the property or give the family the option of naming
  the park. COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA requested that staff attain some history
  regarding the property. VICE CHAIR BAIN stated that the naming could possibly be
  a condition of his donation, associated with the sale of the property to the developer
  and possibly not a gift but a condition of the sale. Community Services Supervisor
  Pinuelas stated that it did not appear that it was a condition of how the City acquired
  the land to name the area Butcher Park and was under the impression that the
  intent was to name it something else but stated that staff would research the issue.
  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas also informed the Commission that the
  Staff would send out the survey and come back with an update along with a list of
  suggested names.

  B.  PERIMETER PATHWAY PROJECT (VERBAL REPORT)

  Management Analyst Slawson provided a brief overview of the project. She
  informed the Commission that the project would begin the following week. She also
  stated that there was an issue acquiring the fitness equipment that was approved
  by the Commission due to a supply issue and that the contractor was looking for
  similar alternatives although it appeared that there may be delay to that portion of
  the project.

  C.  2022 TRACY AUSTIN DOUBLES TENNIS TOURNAMENT DEBRIEF

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
November 14, 2022
   Community Services Coordinator Morrow gave a brief overview of the written
  report.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI requested that an addition be made to the report
  about the recognition of tennis pro Bob Krueger’s service with the tennis tournament
  and to the community.

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated and agreed that it would be a nice touch to provide
  small snack options to the players instead of selling concessions. She
  recommended adding details about the VIP Luncheon to the report as well
  mentioning the attendance and sponsor engagement at the luncheon.

  D.  EQUINE EMERGENCY SHELTER AGREEMENT

  Management Analyst Slawson gave a brief overview of the written report.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN asked about the use of the facility and was happy that the
  County was conducting this kind of planning. She asked how our equestrian
  community would be able to use our facility in the event of an emergency here in
  the City or on the Peninsula and asked how the facility had been evaluated.
  Management Analyst Slawson shared that the County is looking at our facility as a
  shelter in the event of a stable emergency isolated on the other side of the
  Peninsula. She stated that they are also looking at a location in Pomona as a shelter
  facility for the equestrian community on the Peninsula if a large-scale emergency
  occurs in the City. VICE CHAIR BAIN asked if there was reciprocity for our City to
  use these other locations in the event of an emergency. Management Analyst
  Slawson concurred that yes our City can use any location that is designated by the
  County.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA stated that in an emergency it would be difficult for
  the horses to get to Ernie Howlett and also noted that it is an enclosed park and
  would be difficult to remove the horses if needed.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN asked a question regarding fees as the report stated that there
  would be fees but Attachment D stated that there would not be any fees.

  **COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI left the Chambers at 7:47 pm**

  Management Analyst Slawson stated that City Manager Grammar decided that we
  would not charge the County fees for using our facility as a mutual relationship with
  the County. She also stated that there are multiple articles in the MOU stating that
  that the County would need to repair any damages.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
November 14, 2022
   COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  POPE to:

  APPROVE THE RECOMMENDATION OF STAFF REGARDING THE USE
  OF ERNIE HOWLETT PARK AS AN EQUINE EMERGENCY SHELTER.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  E.  2023 PROPOSED SPECIAL EVENT SCHEDULE

  **COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI returned to the Chambers at 7:49 pm**

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of the proposed
  special events and event dates for the upcoming year (2023).

  VICE CHAIR BAIN asked about the Tennis Open House proposed date.
  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas responded that the proposed date was
  Saturday, March 25, 2023, but will be coordinated with tennis pro Bob Krueger
  before finalizing.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked if there would be any other movie nights in
  addition to the City’s movie night events. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas
  stated that a March TBD date was listed on the schedule for a possible Silver Spur
  Little League Movie Night based on a 2022 date, but that Staff had not heard of any
  movie nights for SSLL yet.

  F.  PARADE OF LIGHTS UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Pinuelas gave a brief update on the status of the Holiday
  Parade of Lights scheduled for December 3, 2023.

  8.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  DECEMBER MEETING DATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas recommended the Commission consider
  canceling the upcoming December 19 meeting. She also noted that the standard
  third Monday of the month in January (January 16) fell on Martin Luther King Day
  and wanted to see if the Commission would like to consider adjourning to a
  Tuesday, January 17 date for the meeting in January.

  The Commission affirmed and agreed that the Monday, December 19 meeting
  should be canceled and that Tuesday, January 17 would be best for the January
  meeting unless there would not be a quorum. Community Services Supervisor

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
November 14, 2022
   Pinuelas stated that a special meeting would be held later in January if a quorum
  could not be confirmed for a January 17 meeting.

  9.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA reported that Staff and the Youth Sports
  Subcommittee are working with Silver Spur Little League on cleaning up the areas
  they use at Ernie Howlett Park.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if there was any update regarding the ADA
  ramp at Rockbluff Park. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI also asked about the new
  swing set and when it would be installed and noted the grass looked very dry.
  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas stated that she did not have an update,
  but that staff would update the Commission on the status. CHAIR CIAROLLA
  asked what the plan regarding the ADA ramp was. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI
  stated that it appeared that the ramp was not properly installed to correct ADA
  specifications. CHAIR CIAROLLA and COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated
  concerns regarding the ramp as currently constructed with the caution tape around
  the ramp.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  10.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  RECEIVED AND FILED.
